verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes by re-deriving every formula and running 18 counter-examples through the pinned rustc 1.98.1 oracle (host + wasm32-unknown-unknown/cdylib), including two checks the lane itself lacked: an overflow-checks on/off/default probe at opt-level 3, and a direct FFI probe of a u128 extern "C" signature. Every given check's stdout reproduced exactly, and every SMF/Rust fact traced to midly 0.5.3 (event.rs, primitive.rs) or current doc.rust-lang.org pages held up; nothing was refuted. Systemic weakness: citation precision inside midly and reflexive padding. The two u128-tempo-map recipes cite src/primitive.rs for 'tempo=u24, delta=u28', but that tie is only made in src/event.rs (MetaMessage::Tempo(u24), TrackEvent.delta: u28) -- primitive.rs defines just the generic bit-width wrapper types, forcing me to retrieve the other file to actually confirm the claim. Separately, the generic u128-primitive-type doc page is cited as a stock second source on 5 of 10 recipes regardless of relevance (e.g. the f64-precision and remainder-carry recipes never touch u128), while the one recipe that actually needed an ABI citation (u128 across the wasm extern "C" boundary) cited two sources that never mention FFI/ABI at all and missed doc.rust-lang.org's own i128 'ABI compatibility' note -- which is exactly the passage that explains why wasm32-unknown-unknown (no C/C++ toolchain) leaves u128 there unstable, confirmed live when my counter-example compiled silently into a 3-argument wasm export instead of a clean 1-in/1-out signature.
